description: ARM Cortex-M architecture decomposed. Register set, modes (Thread/Handler, Privileged/Unprivileged), exception model + NVIC, MPU, FPU (M4F/M7), SysTick, DSP extensions, TrustZone-M, BusFault/UsageFault/MemManage faults.

sub_mechanisms.name: cortex_m_register_set
sub_mechanisms.definition: R0-R12 general, R13 (SP), R14 (LR), R15 (PC), xPSR (status). Two stacks: MSP (main) + PSP (process).
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard ARM Thumb-2. PSP enables RTOS isolation (kernel uses MSP). EXC_RETURN encodes which stack to use after exception.

sub_mechanisms.name: thumb_2_instruction_set
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mix of 16-bit + 32-bit instructions. High code density.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cortex-M only executes Thumb-2 (no ARM mode). Dense code = less Flash. Good for tiny MCUs.

sub_mechanisms.name: NVIC_priorities
sub_mechanisms.definition: Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller. Per-interrupt priority. Preemption + sub-priority.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hardware-prioritised. Higher-priority interrupts preempt lower. Sub-priority orders same-priority pending. Standard for Cortex-M.

sub_mechanisms.name: exception_entry_stacking
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hardware stacks R0-R3, R12, LR, PC, xPSR. Other registers saved by handler if used.
sub_mechanisms.why: Deterministic interrupt entry (~12 cycles M3). Hardware saves caller-saved regs; ISR saves rest. Foundation of RT.

sub_mechanisms.name: tail_chaining
sub_mechanisms.definition: Back-to-back pending interrupts: skip stack restore + re-save. Direct handler-to-handler transition.
sub_mechanisms.why: ~6 cycles tail-chain vs ~30 cycles full exit+entry. Major RT benefit. Cortex-M specific.

sub_mechanisms.name: MPU_regions
sub_mechanisms.definition: Memory Protection Unit. 8 (M3/M4) or 16 (M33) regions. Each: address + size + permissions + cacheability.
sub_mechanisms.why: Memory isolation without virtual memory. RTOS uses to isolate tasks. Catches NULL pointer dereferences, stack overflow. Standard.

sub_mechanisms.name: FPU_M4F_M7
sub_mechanisms.definition: Single-precision (M4F) or double-precision (M7) hardware floating point. ARMv7-M FPU extension.
sub_mechanisms.why: 10-100x faster than software float. M4F adds ~50 LE to die; standard now. Many DSP applications need.

sub_mechanisms.name: SysTick_timer
sub_mechanisms.definition: 24-bit countdown timer. Standard across all Cortex-M. Configurable interrupt at zero.
sub_mechanisms.why: Universal RTOS tick source. Each MCU has one. Often used for FreeRTOS tick. Predictable, low overhead.

sub_mechanisms.name: DSP_extensions_M4F
sub_mechanisms.definition: Single-cycle MAC, saturating arithmetic, SIMD (limited). CMSIS-DSP library.
sub_mechanisms.why: Audio, motor control, sensor processing. Enables real-time DSP without dedicated DSP chip. M4F + DSP = workhorse.

sub_mechanisms.name: TrustZone_M
sub_mechanisms.definition: Cortex-M33+: secure + non-secure worlds. Hardware-enforced isolation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Security extension for IoT. Sensitive code (crypto, keys) in secure world. Non-secure can't read. Foundation of secure IoT.

sub_mechanisms.name: fault_exceptions
sub_mechanisms.definition: HardFault, MemManage, BusFault, UsageFault. Each indicates specific error class.
sub_mechanisms.why: Diagnostic information for crashes. UsageFault: division by zero, unaligned access. MemManage: MPU violation. Critical for debugging.

sub_mechanisms.name: wait_for_interrupt_WFI
sub_mechanisms.definition: WFI instruction: enter sleep until interrupt. WFE: until event.
sub_mechanisms.why: Power saving. CPU off, peripheral interrupts wake. Foundation of tickless idle. ~μA power vs mA running.

derivation_rules.name: deterministic_interrupt_entry_critical_for_RT
then: interrupt entry latency is predictable (~12 cycles)
derivation_rules.why: Hardware register stacking. Tail-chaining for back-to-back interrupts. Predictable enables WCET analysis. RT-friendly hardware design.

derivation_rules.name: MPU_enables_RTOS_task_isolation
if: RTOS uses MPU for per-task regions
then: task crashes don't corrupt other tasks
derivation_rules.why: Without: rogue pointer in task A corrupts task B. With: MPU faults invalid access. Important for safety-critical + multi-tenant embedded.

derivation_rules.name: FPU_essential_for_signal_processing_at_runtime
if: application does float math at signal rate
derivation_rules.why: Software float: 100s of cycles per operation. FPU: single cycle. Audio at 48 kHz × 32 ops = 1.5M ops/sec. Without FPU: not viable.

derivation_rules.name: TrustZone_M_for_secure_storage
if: device stores cryptographic keys + sensitive code
derivation_rules.why: Without: app code can read keys, modify crypto. With: secure world isolates. Required for many IoT security standards. M33+ feature.

derivation_rules.name: WFI_enables_battery_years_operation
then: WFI brings down average current dramatically
derivation_rules.why: Running: 5-20 mA. Sleep (WFI): 1-30 μA depending on retention. Average = active% × running + sleep% × sleep. Battery years possible.
